nodes.name: dirichlet_unit_at_one_witness
nodes.summary: An actual unit-at-one lookup supplies its canonical signed unit code; no inverse property is hidden in the predicate.

nodes.name: dirichlet_unit_at_one_from_value
nodes.summary: A genuine lookup with a canonical signed unit value satisfies the two-case unit-at-one predicate.

nodes.name: dirichlet_kronecker_delta_table_restrict
nodes.summary: The same actual delta table restricts to every smaller positive window, without changing its unrelated zeroth value.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_from_right_delta
nodes.summary: One actual right-delta convolution supplies both inverse laws by the already proved finite commutativity theorem.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_symmetric
nodes.summary: Swapping the two actual convolution identities makes the original table an inverse of its inverse.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_actual_tables
nodes.summary: The inverse graph entails actual valid input tables; it is never a vacuous equation between missing lookups.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_zero
nodes.summary: Every pair of actual zero-window tables has a genuine delta witness and both empty positive-domain inverse identities, with no condition at one.

nodes.name: dirichlet_unit_equation_append
nodes.summary: Construct the proper signed remainder, solve its unit-coefficient equation, append the actual new input value and preserve every earlier convolution; the target table is arbitrary.

nodes.name: dirichlet_unit_equation_construct
nodes.summary: Finite induction constructs an actual solution G*F=T for every target table and signed unit F(1), with an arbitrary prescribed G(0), including actual witnesses when N=0.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_from_unit
nodes.summary: Construct an actual delta target and solve the genuine triangular convolution equation; both inverse laws and the independently prescribed zeroth value follow.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_from_unit_at_one
nodes.summary: Either actual canonical unit value at one constructively supplies a finite Dirichlet inverse, with any requested value at zero.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_zero_construct
nodes.summary: The empty positive window has a genuinely constructed inverse for any prescribed zeroth value, without assuming any lookup or unit condition at one.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_construct
nodes.summary: The exact empty-window-or-unit-at-one condition constructs actual inverse witnesses, preserving an arbitrary requested value at zero.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_requires_unit_at_one
nodes.summary: At the genuinely in-domain index one, the actual convolution is a signed product equal to one, forcing the original value to be +1 or -1; the nonempty-domain guard is essential.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_positive_unique
nodes.summary: Associativity and independently constructed delta identities force any two actual inverses to agree at every positive input; neither their codes nor their zero values are identified.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_restrict
nodes.summary: An actual inverse restricts with its actual delta witness to every smaller finite positive window, including zero.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_prefix_compatible
nodes.summary: Independently constructed inverse prefixes have identical represented positive values on their common smaller domain.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_involution
nodes.summary: Taking an actual Dirichlet inverse twice recovers precisely the original positive represented values, with no encoding or zeroth-value uniqueness claim.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_criterion
nodes.summary: An actual finite signed arithmetic table has a Dirichlet inverse exactly when the positive window is empty or its actual value at one is +1 or -1.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_positive_criterion
nodes.summary: On a nonempty positive domain the general constructive inverse criterion is precisely the actual signed unit-at-one condition.

nodes.name: dirichlet_inverse_exists_positive_unique
nodes.summary: Construct an actual inverse with any prescribed zeroth value and prove that every actual inverse agrees with it on all positive inputs, including the genuine empty-window boundary.

nodes.name: Le
nodes.summary: Witness-defined non-strict order on natural numbers.

nodes.name: Lt
nodes.summary: Witness-defined strict order on natural numbers.

nodes.name: SignedUnit
nodes.summary: Exactly the canonical signed codes 2 (+1) and 1 (-1). Its equivalence with an actual signed multiplicative inverse and the affine-equation solver are separately proved, not assumed by this two-case graph.

nodes.name: MatrixMinorFourCode
nodes.summary: One canonical injective doubled-Cantor code for all four signed-minor beta-code parameters.

nodes.name: BetaAt
nodes.summary: x is the bounded beta-decoded value at index i.

nodes.name: SignedDecode
nodes.summary: The original canonical integer code: even 2p denotes p, and odd 2k+1 denotes −(k+1). The decoded positive and negative parts are normalized.

nodes.name: SignedBalance
nodes.summary: The original canonical code z represents the integer difference p−n; these supplied components need not be normalized.

nodes.name: ArithTable
nodes.summary: An actual packed signed table with canonical signed entries through index N, including index zero. It contains no divisor transform or inversion hypothesis.

nodes.name: ArithAt
nodes.summary: Two genuine beta entries of the packed table represent the unique canonical signed value z. Distinct component representations need not be equal.

nodes.name: ArithTableEqual
nodes.summary: Pointwise equality of actual canonical signed lookups below l, not equality of table codes or their positive/negative components.

nodes.name: ArithExtend
nodes.summary: A genuine output signed table through l preserves the represented source values at i<l and records the prescribed signed value z at l. Existence is proved by recoding both beta streams.

nodes.name: ArithPositiveEqual
nodes.summary: Equality of represented values at precisely 0<d<=N. Values at zero are unrestricted, and raw codes or positive/negative representatives are not asserted equal.

nodes.name: SignedAdd
nodes.summary: Actual addition of original canonical signed codes, witnessed by their decoders and balanced equality.

nodes.name: SignedMul
nodes.summary: Actual multiplication of original canonical signed codes; opposite-sign products remain on the negative side of the balance.

nodes.name: Dvd
nodes.summary: The natural number d divides n.

nodes.name: DirichletEntry
nodes.summary: At a positive divisor d, witness n=d*q, read the actual signed values F(d) and G(q), and multiply them. Zero and nondivisors contribute canonical zero without reading either input at zero. Source-table validity is separate.

nodes.name: DirichletPrefix
nodes.summary: An actual signed table M records the independently defined convolution entry at every inclusive index 0<=d<=l. The endpoint l is included and can differ from n; no sum or convolution identity is assumed.

nodes.name: Sum
nodes.summary: z is the sum of a beta-coded prefix of length l.

nodes.name: SignedPrefixSum
nodes.summary: The signed balance of two actual natural finite sums, at exactly the indices 0<=i<l. Existence, uniqueness and representation independence are proved separately.

nodes.name: DirichletSum
nodes.summary: Require n>0, construct a real convolution-summand prefix through n, and take its actual signed fold over exactly S n entries. Zero is outside this sum's input domain; no value is assigned by a unit or inversion formula.

nodes.name: DirichletTable
nodes.summary: Three actual finite signed tables whose output H(n), at every 0<n<=N, is the independently defined convolution sum of F and G. All zero entries are unrestricted; only represented positive values, not table codes, are subsequently proved unique.

nodes.name: KroneckerDeltaTable
nodes.summary: An actual signed table has code 2 at n=1 and code 0 at all other positive n<=N. Its zero entry is unrestricted and N=0 has an empty positive domain. Both convolution unit laws are theorems, not definition premises.

nodes.name: DirichletUnitAtOne
nodes.summary: An actual lookup F(1) has canonical signed code 2 or 1. This direct disjunction contains ArithAt, not a SignedUnit or inverse subformula. Table validity, the finite window bound, and the inverse criterion are separate hypotheses or theorems.

nodes.name: DirichletInverse
nodes.summary: Witness a real Kronecker delta table E and both actual convolution tables F*G=E and G*F=E on 0<n<=N. Their graphs include actual table validity; values at zero remain unrestricted. The unit-at-one criterion is not a definition premise, and its necessity requires N>0; zero-window inverse identities are separately proved for all actual input tables.
